questionSections.instruction: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D. Write the correct letter in boxes 27–31 on your answer sheet.
questionSections.instructionZh: 选择正确字母A、B、C或D，并将答案写在答题纸第27—31格。

questions.prompt: In the first paragraph, the writer says that most managers
questions.promptZh: 在第一段中，作者说大多数管理者……

options.A: fail to spot the key consumer trends of the moment.
options.B: make the mistake of focusing only on the principal consumer trends.
options.C: misinterpret market research data relating to current consumer trends.
options.D: are unaware of the significant impact that trends have on consumers’ lives.

optionTranslations.A: 未能发现当下主要的消费者趋势。
optionTranslations.B: 错误地只关注主要的消费者趋势。
optionTranslations.C: 误解了与当前消费者趋势有关的市场调研数据。
optionTranslations.D: 没有意识到趋势对消费者生活所产生的重大影响。

questions.evidence: managers often fail to recognize the less obvious but profound ways these trends are influencing consumers’ aspirations, attitudes, and behaviors
questions.distractors: A/B confuse identifying major trends with understanding their deeper influence; C invents misinterpretation of data.

questions.prompt: According to the third paragraph, Coach was anxious to
questions.promptZh: 根据第三段，Coach急于……

options.A: follow what some of its competitors were doing.
options.B: maintain its prices throughout its range.
options.C: safeguard its reputation as a manufacturer of luxury goods.
options.D: modify the entire look of its brand to suit the economic climate.

optionTranslations.A: 仿效一些竞争对手的做法。
optionTranslations.B: 维持其所有产品的价格。
optionTranslations.C: 维护其奢侈品制造商的声誉。
optionTranslations.D: 改变整个品牌形象以适应经济环境。

questions.evidence: that would have risked cheapening the brand’s image
questions.distractors: A is contradicted by Coach’s contrast with price-cutters; B says the whole range, whereas a lower-priced sub-brand was launched; D overstates the limited sub-brand change.

questions.prompt: What point is made about Tesco’s Greener Living programme?
questions.promptZh: 关于Tesco的Greener Living计划，文中提出了什么观点？

options.A: It did not require Tesco to modify its core business activities.
options.B: It succeeded in attracting a more eco-conscious clientele.
options.C: Its main aim was to raise consumers’ awareness of environmental issues.
options.D: It was not the first time that Tesco had implemented such an initiative.

optionTranslations.A: 它不要求Tesco改变核心业务活动。
optionTranslations.B: 它成功吸引了环保意识更强的客户群。
optionTranslations.C: 其主要目标是提高消费者对环境问题的认识。
optionTranslations.D: 这并非Tesco首次实施此类举措。

questions.evidence: Tesco has not abandoned its traditional retail offerings but augmented its business with these innovations
questions.distractors: B gives an unreported outcome; C substitutes awareness for tangible participation; D has no supporting comparison with an earlier initiative.

questions.prompt: What does the writer suggest about Nike’s strategy?
questions.promptZh: 作者对Nike的策略有何暗示？

options.A: It was an extremely risky strategy at the time.
options.B: It was a strategy that only a major company could afford to follow.
options.C: It was the type of strategy that would not have been possible in the past.
options.D: It was the kind of strategy which might appear to have few obvious benefits.

optionTranslations.A: 当时这是一项风险极高的策略。
optionTranslations.B: 只有大公司才负担得起这种策略。
optionTranslations.C: 这种策略在过去不可能实现。
optionTranslations.D: 这种策略看起来可能没有多少明显好处。

questions.evidence: sounds like it’s hardly worthwhile. But consider Nike’s move
questions.distractors: A, B and C are not stated; the text specifically frames the move as seemingly hardly worthwhile.

questions.prompt: What was original about the ME2?
questions.promptZh: ME2的创新之处是什么？

options.A: It contained technology that had been developed for the sports industry.
options.B: It appealed to young people who were keen to improve their physical fitness.
options.C: It took advantage of a current trend for video games with colourful 3D graphics.
options.D: It was a handheld game that addressed people’s concerns about unhealthy lifestyles.

optionTranslations.A: 它采用了为体育产业开发的技术。
optionTranslations.B: 它吸引了热衷改善体能的年轻人。
optionTranslations.C: 它利用了彩色3D图像电子游戏的流行趋势。
optionTranslations.D: 它是一款回应人们对不健康生活方式担忧的掌上游戏。

questions.evidence: countering the negatives, such as associations with lack of exercise and obesity
questions.distractors: A gives an unsupported origin for the pedometer; B mistakes the mechanism for users’ motive; C describes a conventional feature, not what set ME2 apart.

questionSections.instruction: Look at the following statements (Questions 32–37) and the list of companies below. Match each statement with the correct company, A, B, C or D. Write the correct letter, A, B, C or D, in boxes 32–37 on your answer sheet. NB You may use any letter more than once.
questionSections.instructionZh: 阅读第32—37题陈述和下方公司列表，把每项陈述与正确公司A、B、C或D配对；同一字母可以使用多次。

questions.prompt: It turned the notion that its products could have harmful effects to its own advantage.
questions.promptZh: 它把其产品可能产生有害影响的观念转化成了自身优势。
questions.evidence: the ME2 counteracted some of the widely perceived negative impacts of digital gaming devices
questions.distractors: Coach addresses recession, Tesco environmental concern, and Nike the digital revolution; only iToys directly turns gaming’s unhealthy associations into a differentiator.

questions.prompt: It extended its offering by collaborating with another manufacturer.
questions.promptZh: 它通过与另一家制造商合作扩展了自身产品。
questions.evidence: they teamed up with technology company Apple to launch Nike+
questions.distractors: No partnership with another manufacturer is stated for Coach, Tesco or iToys.

questions.prompt: It implemented an incentive scheme to demonstrate its corporate social responsibility.
questions.promptZh: 它实施了一项激励计划来体现企业社会责任。
questions.evidence: Tesco customers can accumulate points ... these green points can be redeemed for cash
questions.distractors: The other companies launch products; only Tesco rewards environmentally helpful customer actions.

questions.prompt: It discovered that customers had a positive attitude towards dealing with difficult circumstances.
questions.promptZh: 它发现顾客对克服困境持积极态度。
questions.evidence: customers were eager to lift themselves and the country out of tough times
questions.distractors: The finding comes from Coach’s consumer research, not the other three cases.

questions.prompt: It responded to a growing lifestyle trend in an unrelated product sector.
questions.promptZh: 它回应了一个来自无关产品领域、不断增长的生活方式趋势。
questions.evidence: integrate the digital revolution into its reputation for high-performance athletic footwear
questions.distractors: Nike combines footwear with the digital sector; the other examples remain tied to price, retail environmentalism, or gaming’s physical effects.

questions.prompt: It successfully avoided having to charge its customers less for its core products.
questions.promptZh: 它成功避免了不得不降低核心产品售价。
questions.evidence: Creating the sub-brand allowed Coach to avert an across-the-board price cut.
questions.distractors: Only Coach is described as avoiding a price cut across its established range.

questionSections.instruction: Complete each sentence with the correct ending, A, B, C or D below. Write the correct letter, A, B, C or D, in boxes 38–40 on your answer sheet.
questionSections.instructionZh: 从下方A、B、C或D中选择正确结尾补全每个句子，并将字母写在答题纸第38—40格。

options.A: employ a combination of strategies to maintain your consumer base.
options.B: identify the most appropriate innovation strategy to use.
options.C: emphasise your brand’s traditional values with the counteract-and-affirm strategy.
options.D: use the combine-and-transcend strategy to integrate the two worlds.

optionTranslations.A: 采用多种策略的组合来维持消费者基础。
optionTranslations.B: 确定最适合采用的创新策略。
optionTranslations.C: 运用‘抵消并确认’策略强调品牌的传统价值。
optionTranslations.D: 运用‘结合并超越’策略整合两个世界。

questions.prompt: If there are any trend-related changes impacting on your category, you should
questions.promptZh: 如果存在任何影响你所在品类的趋势相关变化，你应该……
questions.evidence: you can determine which of our three innovation strategies to pursue
questions.distractors: A is never advised; C and D apply only after a specific relationship between trend and category is diagnosed.

questions.prompt: If a current trend highlights a negative aspect of your category, you should
questions.promptZh: 如果当前趋势凸显了你所在品类的负面方面，你应该……
questions.evidence: if aspects of the category clash with undesired outcomes of a trend ... counteract those changes by reaffirming the core values
questions.distractors: B is the preliminary general step; D is for disparity, while A is unsupported.

questions.prompt: If the consumers’ new focus has an increasing lack of connection with your offering, you should
questions.promptZh: 如果消费者的新关注点与你的产品越来越脱节，你应该……
questions.evidence: an increasing disparity between your category and consumers’ new focus ... transcend the category to integrate the two worlds
questions.distractors: C applies to undesirable outcomes, B is nonspecific, and A is not a stated recommendation.

questions.evidence: an ingredient that was mixed with oils for anointing people’s bodies
questions.explanation: added to 改写 mixed with；空格需要复数名词，原文为 oils。
questions.distractorAnalysis: ingredient 是肉桂所充当的角色，不是它被加入的对象；bodies 是涂抹对象。

questions.promptZh: 用于表示人与人之间的__________
questions.evidence: as a token indicating friendship among lovers and friends
questions.explanation: show 对应 indicating，between people 概括 among lovers and friends，因此填 friendship。
questions.distractorAnalysis: token 是表达友谊的载体，题干问所表达的关系；lovers 只是一类人。

questions.prompt: used for its sweet smell at 3 __________
questions.promptZh: 在__________中因其芳香而被使用
questions.evidence: mourners attending funerals burnt cinnamon to create a pleasant scent
questions.explanation: sweet smell 对应 pleasant scent；使用场合是 funerals。
questions.distractorAnalysis: mourners 是参与者，不是 at 后的场合；Rome 已由时间栏目给出。

questions.prompt: was an indication of a person’s 4 __________
questions.promptZh: 是一个人__________的象征
questions.evidence: as a sign of the wealth at his or her disposal
questions.explanation: indication 对应 sign，a person’s 对应 his or her；答案为 wealth。
questions.distractorAnalysis: ability 是购买昂贵香料的能力，但宴会陈列直接作为财富的标志；spices 是展示物。

questions.prompt: known as a treatment for 5 __________ and other health problems
questions.promptZh: 被视为治疗__________及其他健康问题的一种疗法
questions.evidence: was thought to cure various ailments, such as indigestion
questions.explanation: treatment for 改写 cure；and other health problems 表明空格要填示例病症 indigestion。
questions.distractorAnalysis: ailments 是上位概念，若填入会形成“病症及其他健康问题”的泛化，题干要求具体例子。

questions.evidence: They took it from India, where it was grown
questions.explanation: where 指代 India，直接说明肉桂种植地。
questions.distractorAnalysis: Ceylon 是后文15世纪末葡萄牙人抵达的产区，不是本组早期阿拉伯运输路线的起点。

questions.prompt: merchants used 7 __________ to bring it to the Mediterranean
questions.promptZh: 商人用__________把它运到地中海
questions.evidence: on camels via an overland route to the Mediterranean
questions.explanation: used 提示工具，on camels 表运输工具；ONE WORD ONLY 填 camels。
questions.distractorAnalysis: route 是路径而不是承载工具；merchants 已在题干中。

questions.promptZh: 在__________抵达地中海地区
questions.evidence: Their journey ended when they reached Alexandria.
questions.explanation: journey ended/reached 对应 arrived；地中海陆路终点是 Alexandria。
questions.distractorAnalysis: India 是起点；Venice 是欧洲商人随后带回香料的城市。

questions.prompt: traders took it to 9 __________ and sold it to destinations around Europe
questions.promptZh: 商人把它运到__________，再销往欧洲各地
questions.evidence: brought it back to Venice. The spice then travelled from that great trading city to markets all around Europe.
questions.explanation: took it to 对应 brought it back to；随后从该贸易城市分销欧洲，故填 Venice。
questions.distractorAnalysis: Alexandria 是欧洲商人采购地点，不是向欧洲各地分销的贸易城市。

questions.prompt: The Portuguese had control over the cinnamon trade in Ceylon throughout the 16th century.
questions.promptZh: 整个16世纪，葡萄牙人一直控制着锡兰的肉桂贸易。
questions.evidence: Portuguese traders arrived ... toward the end of the 15th century. In 1518, the Portuguese built a fort ... helping them to develop a monopoly ... By 1640, the Dutch broke the 150-year Portuguese monopoly
questions.explanation: 葡萄牙人在15世纪末已进入，1518年建立控制，而荷兰到1640年才打破垄断，因此16世纪全程处在其控制期。
questions.distractorAnalysis: FALSE 会把荷兰17世纪初到达误当成当即接管；NOT GIVEN 忽略了时间链和150年垄断。

questions.prompt: The Dutch took over the cinnamon trade from the Portuguese as soon as they arrived in Ceylon.
questions.promptZh: 荷兰人一到锡兰就立即从葡萄牙人手中接管了肉桂贸易。
questions.evidence: When the Dutch arrived ... at the very beginning of the 17th century ... By 1640, the Dutch broke the 150-year Portuguese monopoly
questions.explanation: arrived 在17世纪初，break monopoly 到1640年，中间还需结盟与作战；并非 as soon as。
questions.distractorAnalysis: TRUE 利用 arrived/took over 的同主题词，却忽略时间差；NOT GIVEN 不成立，因为两个时间点明确。

questions.prompt: The trees planted by the Dutch produced larger quantities of cinnamon than the wild trees.
questions.promptZh: 荷兰人种植的肉桂树比野生肉桂树产量更大。
questions.evidence: the Dutch began cultivating their own cinnamon trees to supplement the diminishing number of wild trees available for use
questions.explanation: 原文只说人工栽培用于补充数量减少的野生树，没有比较两类树的产量。
questions.distractorAnalysis: TRUE 把 supplement 偷换成“产量更大”；FALSE 同样需要反向产量比较，但原文没有。

questions.prompt: The spice trade maintained its economic importance during the 19th century.
questions.promptZh: 在19世纪，香料贸易一直保持其经济重要性。
questions.evidence: the spice trade overall was diminishing in economic potential, and was eventually superseded by the rise of trade in coffee, tea, chocolate, and sugar
questions.explanation: maintained economic importance 与 diminishing in economic potential 并 eventually superseded 直接矛盾。
questions.distractorAnalysis: TRUE 可能被19世纪肉桂产量上升误导，但题干问整个香料贸易的经济重要性；NOT GIVEN 不成立，因为原文明确评价其衰退。

questions.stem: reference to research showing the beneficial effects of oxytocin on people
questions.stemZh: 提到显示催产素对人有益的研究
questions.evidence: These follow-up studies have shown that after a sniff of the hormone, people become more charitable, better at reading emotions on others’ faces and at communicating constructively in arguments.
questions.reasoning: beneficial effects 对应 charitable、better at reading emotions、communicating constructively。
questions.distractors: A主要是动物与早期正面声誉；题干明确说 research 与 people，B直接列出后续人体研究结果。
questions.prompt: reference to research showing the beneficial effects of oxytocin on people
questions.promptZh: 提到显示催产素对人有益的研究
questions.explanation: beneficial effects 对应 charitable、better at reading emotions、communicating constructively。
questions.distractorAnalysis: A主要是动物与早期正面声誉；题干明确说 research 与 people，B直接列出后续人体研究结果。

questions.stem: reasons why the effects of oxytocin are complex
questions.stemZh: 催产素作用复杂的原因
questions.evidence: It’s a very simple and ancient molecule that has been co-opted for many different functions ... once you add our higher-order thinking and social situations, these basic processes could manifest in different ways depending on individual differences and context.
questions.reasoning: many different functions、higher-order thinking、social situations、individual differences 和 context 共同解释复杂性。
questions.distractors: E讨论寻找核心机制及假说，不是集中说明复杂性的成因。
questions.prompt: reasons why the effects of oxytocin are complex
questions.promptZh: 催产素作用复杂的原因
questions.explanation: many different functions、higher-order thinking、social situations、individual differences 和 context 共同解释复杂性。
questions.distractorAnalysis: E讨论寻找核心机制及假说，不是集中说明复杂性的成因。

questions.stem: mention of a period in which oxytocin attracted little scientific attention
questions.stemZh: 提到催产素很少受到科学界关注的一段时期
questions.evidence: ‘For eight years, it was quite a lonesome field,’ Heinrichs recalls.
questions.reasoning: a lonesome field 表示这一研究领域当时参与者少，对应 little scientific attention。
questions.distractors: F谈历史悠久而非科学关注度；E说忽略某些研究发现，含义不同。
questions.prompt: mention of a period in which oxytocin attracted little scientific attention
questions.promptZh: 提到催产素很少受到科学界关注的一段时期
questions.explanation: a lonesome field 表示这一研究领域当时参与者少，对应 little scientific attention。
questions.distractorAnalysis: F谈历史悠久而非科学关注度；E说忽略某些研究发现，含义不同。

questions.stem: reference to people ignoring certain aspects of their research data
questions.stemZh: 提到研究人员忽视其研究数据的某些方面
questions.evidence: Where once researchers took no notice of such findings, now a more nuanced understanding of oxytocin’s effects is propelling investigations down new lines.
questions.reasoning: took no notice of such findings 直接同义替换 ignoring certain aspects of research data。
questions.distractors: B是领域受冷落；题干则是研究者忽略已经出现的结果。
questions.prompt: reference to people ignoring certain aspects of their research data
questions.promptZh: 提到研究人员忽视其研究数据的某些方面
questions.explanation: took no notice of such findings 直接同义替换 ignoring certain aspects of research data。
questions.distractorAnalysis: B是领域受冷落；题干则是研究者忽略已经出现的结果。

questions.stem: People are more trusting when affected by oxytocin.
questions.stemZh: 人们受催产素影响时会更加信任他人。
questions.evidence: The team found that participants who had sniffed oxytocin via a nasal spray beforehand invested more money than those who received a placebo instead.
questions.reasoning: 愿意向无法保证诚实的匿名对象投入更多钱，体现 more trusting；该实验由 Heinrichs 团队完成。
questions.distractors: B研究竞争中的嫉妒；C研究个体差异；D研究陌生人合作；E研究内群体偏爱；F解释进化与脑机制。
questions.prompt: People are more trusting when affected by oxytocin.
questions.promptZh: 人们受催产素影响时会更加信任他人。
questions.explanation: 愿意向无法保证诚实的匿名对象投入更多钱，体现 more trusting；该实验由 Heinrichs 团队完成。
questions.distractorAnalysis: B研究竞争中的嫉妒；C研究个体差异；D研究陌生人合作；E研究内群体偏爱；F解释进化与脑机制。

questions.stem: Oxytocin increases people’s feelings of jealousy.
questions.stemZh: 催产素增强人的嫉妒感。
questions.evidence: Simone Shamay-Tsoory ... found that ... those who inhaled the hormone ... felt more envy when others won.
questions.reasoning: jealousy 与原文 envy 同义，研究者是 Simone Shamay-Tsoory。
questions.distractors: 其余研究者的发现分别涉及信任、识别情绪、陌生人合作、偏爱和机制。
questions.prompt: Oxytocin increases people’s feelings of jealousy.
questions.promptZh: 催产素增强人的嫉妒感。
questions.explanation: jealousy 与原文 envy 同义，研究者是 Simone Shamay-Tsoory。
questions.distractorAnalysis: 其余研究者的发现分别涉及信任、识别情绪、陌生人合作、偏爱和机制。

questions.stem: The effect of oxytocin varies from one type of person to another.
questions.stemZh: 催产素的作用因人而异。
questions.evidence: Jennifer Bartz ... found that it improves people’s ability to read emotions, but only if they are not very socially adept to begin with.
questions.reasoning: only if 限定某一类人，说明作用随人的类型而变化。
questions.distractors: D、E考查互动对象或群体偏向，不是受试者本人的类型差异。
questions.prompt: The effect of oxytocin varies from one type of person to another.
questions.promptZh: 催产素的作用因人而异。
questions.explanation: only if 限定某一类人，说明作用随人的类型而变化。
questions.distractorAnalysis: D、E考查互动对象或群体偏向，不是受试者本人的类型差异。

questions.stem: The earliest findings about oxytocin and bonding came from research involving ________.
questions.stemZh: 关于催产素与情感联结的最早发现来自涉及________的研究。
questions.evidence: It was through various studies focusing on animals that scientists first became aware of the influence of oxytocin.
questions.reasoning: research involving 对应 studies focusing on；答案 animals 为原文一个词。
questions.distractors: prairie voles 和 sheep 是具体例子，但概括空需要上位词 animals。
questions.prompt: The earliest findings about oxytocin and bonding came from research involving ________.
questions.promptZh: 关于催产素与情感联结的最早发现来自涉及________的研究。
questions.explanation: research involving 对应 studies focusing on；答案 animals 为原文一个词。
questions.distractorAnalysis: prairie voles 和 sheep 是具体例子，但概括空需要上位词 animals。

questions.stem: It was also discovered that humans produce oxytocin during ________.
questions.stemZh: 研究还发现，人类在________期间会产生催产素。
questions.evidence: It is also released by women in childbirth, strengthening the attachment between mother and baby.
questions.reasoning: produce oxytocin 对应 is released；during 对应 in，填 childbirth。
questions.distractors: attachment 是释放后的作用，不是发生时间。
questions.prompt: It was also discovered that humans produce oxytocin during ________.
questions.promptZh: 研究还发现，人类在________期间会产生催产素。
questions.explanation: produce oxytocin 对应 is released；during 对应 in，填 childbirth。
questions.distractorAnalysis: attachment 是释放后的作用，不是发生时间。

questions.stem: An experiment in 2005, in which participants were given either oxytocin or a ________, reinforced the belief that the hormone had a positive effect.
questions.stemZh: 2005年的实验给参与者使用催产素或________，强化了该激素有积极作用的看法。
questions.evidence: The team found that participants who had sniffed oxytocin via a nasal spray beforehand invested more money than those who received a placebo instead.
questions.reasoning: either oxytocin or 与原文 oxytocin 组和 placebo 对照组对应。
questions.distractors: spray 是给药方式；placebo 才是与 oxytocin 对照的物质。
questions.prompt: An experiment in 2005, in which participants were given either oxytocin or a ________, reinforced the belief that the hormone had a positive effect.
questions.promptZh: 2005年的实验给参与者使用催产素或________，强化了该激素有积极作用的看法。
questions.explanation: either oxytocin or 与原文 oxytocin 组和 placebo 对照组对应。
questions.distractorAnalysis: spray 是给药方式；placebo 才是与 oxytocin 对照的物质。

questions.stem: A study at the University of Haifa where participants took part in a ________, revealed the negative emotions which oxytocin can trigger.
questions.stemZh: 海法大学的研究让参与者参加一场________，揭示了催产素可能触发的负面情绪。
questions.evidence: Simone Shamay-Tsoory at the University of Haifa, Israel, found that when volunteers played a competitive game ... felt more envy when others won.
questions.reasoning: took part in 对应 played；冠词 a 后填单数名词 game。
questions.distractors: competitive 虽在原文出现，但它是形容词，无法单独充当 a 后的中心名词。
questions.prompt: A study at the University of Haifa where participants took part in a ________, revealed the negative emotions which oxytocin can trigger.
questions.promptZh: 海法大学的研究让参与者参加一场________，揭示了催产素可能触发的负面情绪。
questions.explanation: took part in 对应 played；冠词 a 后填单数名词 game。
questions.distractorAnalysis: competitive 虽在原文出现，但它是形容词，无法单独充当 a 后的中心名词。

questions.stem: A study at the University of Antwerp showed people’s lack of willingness to help ________ while under the influence of oxytocin.
questions.stemZh: 安特卫普大学的研究显示，人在催产素影响下不愿帮助________。
questions.evidence: Studies conducted by Carolyn DeClerck of the University of Antwerp, Belgium, revealed that people who had received a dose of oxytocin actually became less cooperative when dealing with complete strangers.
questions.reasoning: lack of willingness to help 对应 less cooperative；对象为 strangers。
questions.distractors: complete 是修饰词；只能填一词且语义中心是 strangers。
questions.prompt: A study at the University of Antwerp showed people’s lack of willingness to help ________ while under the influence of oxytocin.
questions.promptZh: 安特卫普大学的研究显示，人在催产素影响下不愿帮助________。
questions.explanation: lack of willingness to help 对应 less cooperative；对象为 strangers。
questions.distractorAnalysis: complete 是修饰词；只能填一词且语义中心是 strangers。

questions.stem: People who have been given oxytocin consider ________ that are familiar to them in their own country to have more positive associations than those from other cultures.
questions.stemZh: 使用催产素的人认为本国熟悉的________比其他文化中的对应事物有更积极的联想。
questions.evidence: Dutch men became quicker to associate positive words with Dutch names than with foreign ones, for example.
questions.reasoning: familiar in their own country 对应 Dutch；those from other cultures 对应 foreign ones，比较对象是 names。
questions.distractors: words 是被联想到的 positive 内容；实际被比较的是 Dutch names 与 foreign ones。
questions.prompt: People who have been given oxytocin consider ________ that are familiar to them in their own country to have more positive associations than those from other cultures.
questions.promptZh: 使用催产素的人认为本国熟悉的________比其他文化中的对应事物有更积极的联想。
questions.explanation: familiar in their own country 对应 Dutch；those from other cultures 对应 foreign ones，比较对象是 names。
questions.distractorAnalysis: words 是被联想到的 positive 内容；实际被比较的是 Dutch names 与 foreign ones。

questions.prompt: In the first paragraph, the writer says that most managers
questions.promptZh: 在第一段中，作者说大多数管理者……

options.A: fail to spot the key consumer trends of the moment.
options.B: make the mistake of focusing only on the principal consumer trends.
options.C: misinterpret market research data relating to current consumer trends.
options.D: are unaware of the significant impact that trends have on consumers’ lives.

optionTranslations.A: 未能发现当下主要的消费者趋势。
optionTranslations.B: 错误地只关注主要的消费者趋势。
optionTranslations.C: 误解了与当前消费者趋势有关的市场调研数据。
optionTranslations.D: 没有意识到趋势对消费者生活所产生的重大影响。

questions.evidence: managers often fail to recognize the less obvious but profound ways these trends are influencing consumers’ aspirations, attitudes, and behaviors
questions.distractors: A/B confuse identifying major trends with understanding their deeper influence; C invents misinterpretation of data.

questions.prompt: According to the third paragraph, Coach was anxious to
questions.promptZh: 根据第三段，Coach急于……

options.A: follow what some of its competitors were doing.
options.B: maintain its prices throughout its range.
options.C: safeguard its reputation as a manufacturer of luxury goods.
options.D: modify the entire look of its brand to suit the economic climate.

optionTranslations.A: 仿效一些竞争对手的做法。
optionTranslations.B: 维持其所有产品的价格。
optionTranslations.C: 维护其奢侈品制造商的声誉。
optionTranslations.D: 改变整个品牌形象以适应经济环境。

questions.evidence: that would have risked cheapening the brand’s image
questions.distractors: A is contradicted by Coach’s contrast with price-cutters; B says the whole range, whereas a lower-priced sub-brand was launched; D overstates the limited sub-brand change.

questions.prompt: What point is made about Tesco’s Greener Living programme?
questions.promptZh: 关于Tesco的Greener Living计划，文中提出了什么观点？

options.A: It did not require Tesco to modify its core business activities.
options.B: It succeeded in attracting a more eco-conscious clientele.
options.C: Its main aim was to raise consumers’ awareness of environmental issues.
options.D: It was not the first time that Tesco had implemented such an initiative.

optionTranslations.A: 它不要求Tesco改变核心业务活动。
optionTranslations.B: 它成功吸引了环保意识更强的客户群。
optionTranslations.C: 其主要目标是提高消费者对环境问题的认识。
optionTranslations.D: 这并非Tesco首次实施此类举措。

questions.evidence: Tesco has not abandoned its traditional retail offerings but augmented its business with these innovations
questions.distractors: B gives an unreported outcome; C substitutes awareness for tangible participation; D has no supporting comparison with an earlier initiative.

questions.prompt: What does the writer suggest about Nike’s strategy?
questions.promptZh: 作者对Nike的策略有何暗示？

options.A: It was an extremely risky strategy at the time.
options.B: It was a strategy that only a major company could afford to follow.
options.C: It was the type of strategy that would not have been possible in the past.
options.D: It was the kind of strategy which might appear to have few obvious benefits.

optionTranslations.A: 当时这是一项风险极高的策略。
optionTranslations.B: 只有大公司才负担得起这种策略。
optionTranslations.C: 这种策略在过去不可能实现。
optionTranslations.D: 这种策略看起来可能没有多少明显好处。

questions.evidence: sounds like it’s hardly worthwhile. But consider Nike’s move
questions.distractors: A, B and C are not stated; the text specifically frames the move as seemingly hardly worthwhile.

questions.prompt: What was original about the ME2?
questions.promptZh: ME2的创新之处是什么？

options.A: It contained technology that had been developed for the sports industry.
options.B: It appealed to young people who were keen to improve their physical fitness.
options.C: It took advantage of a current trend for video games with colourful 3D graphics.
options.D: It was a handheld game that addressed people’s concerns about unhealthy lifestyles.

optionTranslations.A: 它采用了为体育产业开发的技术。
optionTranslations.B: 它吸引了热衷改善体能的年轻人。
optionTranslations.C: 它利用了彩色3D图像电子游戏的流行趋势。
optionTranslations.D: 它是一款回应人们对不健康生活方式担忧的掌上游戏。

questions.evidence: countering the negatives, such as associations with lack of exercise and obesity
questions.distractors: A gives an unsupported origin for the pedometer; B mistakes the mechanism for users’ motive; C describes a conventional feature, not what set ME2 apart.

questions.prompt: It turned the notion that its products could have harmful effects to its own advantage.
questions.promptZh: 它把其产品可能产生有害影响的观念转化成了自身优势。
questions.evidence: the ME2 counteracted some of the widely perceived negative impacts of digital gaming devices
questions.distractors: Coach addresses recession, Tesco environmental concern, and Nike the digital revolution; only iToys directly turns gaming’s unhealthy associations into a differentiator.

questions.prompt: It extended its offering by collaborating with another manufacturer.
questions.promptZh: 它通过与另一家制造商合作扩展了自身产品。
questions.evidence: they teamed up with technology company Apple to launch Nike+
questions.distractors: No partnership with another manufacturer is stated for Coach, Tesco or iToys.

questions.prompt: It implemented an incentive scheme to demonstrate its corporate social responsibility.
questions.promptZh: 它实施了一项激励计划来体现企业社会责任。
questions.evidence: Tesco customers can accumulate points ... these green points can be redeemed for cash
questions.distractors: The other companies launch products; only Tesco rewards environmentally helpful customer actions.

questions.prompt: It discovered that customers had a positive attitude towards dealing with difficult circumstances.
questions.promptZh: 它发现顾客对克服困境持积极态度。
questions.evidence: customers were eager to lift themselves and the country out of tough times
questions.distractors: The finding comes from Coach’s consumer research, not the other three cases.

questions.prompt: It responded to a growing lifestyle trend in an unrelated product sector.
questions.promptZh: 它回应了一个来自无关产品领域、不断增长的生活方式趋势。
questions.evidence: integrate the digital revolution into its reputation for high-performance athletic footwear
questions.distractors: Nike combines footwear with the digital sector; the other examples remain tied to price, retail environmentalism, or gaming’s physical effects.

questions.prompt: It successfully avoided having to charge its customers less for its core products.
questions.promptZh: 它成功避免了不得不降低核心产品售价。
questions.evidence: Creating the sub-brand allowed Coach to avert an across-the-board price cut.
questions.distractors: Only Coach is described as avoiding a price cut across its established range.

questions.prompt: If there are any trend-related changes impacting on your category, you should
questions.promptZh: 如果存在任何影响你所在品类的趋势相关变化，你应该……
questions.evidence: you can determine which of our three innovation strategies to pursue
questions.distractors: A is never advised; C and D apply only after a specific relationship between trend and category is diagnosed.

questions.prompt: If a current trend highlights a negative aspect of your category, you should
questions.promptZh: 如果当前趋势凸显了你所在品类的负面方面，你应该……
questions.evidence: if aspects of the category clash with undesired outcomes of a trend ... counteract those changes by reaffirming the core values
questions.distractors: B is the preliminary general step; D is for disparity, while A is unsupported.

questions.prompt: If the consumers’ new focus has an increasing lack of connection with your offering, you should
questions.promptZh: 如果消费者的新关注点与你的产品越来越脱节，你应该……
questions.evidence: an increasing disparity between your category and consumers’ new focus ... transcend the category to integrate the two worlds
questions.distractors: C applies to undesirable outcomes, B is nonspecific, and A is not a stated recommendation.

SAMPLE ANSWER
This is an answer written by a candidate who achieved a Band 5.5 score. Here is the
examiner's comment:
The candidate has identified all the key features (hospital, ring road, new public
car park, staff car park and bus station in 2010) but the descriptions are not always
accurate e.g. [two features that still remained. This two features are City Hospital
and staff car park] whereas the staff car park was formerly a car park for both staff
and public, while the mention of the bus station is not developed. Organisation is
clear, however, with some good use of cohesive devices [According to  Apart from
The further additional features], although there is an error in the use of reference
pronouns [This/These two features]. The range of vocabulary is sufficient for the
task [two different years | features | remained | additional], though [features] is
over-used. A spelling error is noted in the second line [sourrounded] but this
does not cause any difficulty for the reader; similarly, the use of [around-turn]
can be easily understood as 'roundabout'. There is a mix of simple and complex
sentences, mainly used accurately.
Two maps illustrate the way to get to a city hospital of two different years (2oo7 and 2010).
According to both maps, the main features which is city hospital is sourrounded by Ring Road. In
these two maps, there have been two features that still remained. This two features are City Hospital
and staff car park. Apart from these two features there are some features that shows on 2olo map
but haven't shown on 2007 map. The additional features that appear on the map of 2010 are public
car park which located on the east-side of the city hospital. The further additional features are two
around-turn on the hospital Rd. which can lead to the bus station.
Overall, there are two major features that never change on both 2007 and 2010 map. These features
are city hospital and staff car park. However, there are some additional features that appear
on the map of 2oio but not on 2oo7. These features are public car park, bus station and two
around-turns.

Sample answers for Writing tasks
TEST 1, WRITING TASK 2
SAMPLE ANSWER
This is an answer written by a candidate who achieved a Band 6.5 score. Here is the
examiner's comment:
The candidate deals with both parts of the prompt and addresses some social and
practical problems that might be experienced in a foreign language environment.
Ideas are supported by examples, though there is room for further development
here. Organisation is logical and there is clear progression throughout the
response. Cohesive devices are used appropriately [Another problem | For
example | Therefore | That means ... | The second ... problem | To summarize].
There is a sufficient range of vocabulary to allow some flexibility and precision and
to demonstrate awareness of style and collocation [language barrier linked to
influence the behaviour | offend | misunderstanding | misconceptions]. There is a
mix of simple and complex sentence forms including subordinate clauses [which
means that | a person who], modal verbs [should | might | would] and gerunds
[finding a job]. Grammatical control is generally good as is the use of punctuation,
although the first sentence in the second paragraph is incomplete.
It is clear that living in a foreign country has its own benefits and drawbacks to consider. I agre
with this statement, however I think that anybody coming in another country should respect national
culture. In this essay, I would like to outline the social and practical problems.
The social problems would be language barrier, which means that a person coming from another
country might not be able to speak and understand the language which might be a problem as far
a person who is living in a country, and a person who came in the country. Another problem is
linked to the language barrier, but it might influence the behaviour of others. An individual who
come into the country might offend others with their behaviour or language. For example; some
cultures like English people prefer to be very polite and say things differently from other cultures.
Therefore a person who doesn't know how to behave in a particular culture might offend others
around him.
The practical problems would be misunderstanding of culture. That means that a person who visits
other countries does not understand other culture and he behaves as he wants to.
The second practical problem is finding a job. An individual who works in foreign country might not
be appropriate for people who he serves. For example if an individual works in a restaurant, the
people who live in a country and they were born in that country might not respect and not like the
behaviour of a person who works in a restaurant, it might be because, the cultures are different.
To summarize, it can be said that there are a lot of misconceptions which people have when they
come in a foreign country, and in my opinion and from my personal experience people should
educate themselves in order to know how to behave in different situations with different cultures.
127

TEST 2, WRITING TASK 2
SAMPLE ANSWER
This is an answer written by a candidate who achieved a Band 7.0 score. Here is the
examiner's comment:
The candidate explains why s/he both agrees and disagrees with the statement,
meeting the requirements of 'To what extent do you agree or disagree with this
statement?' S/he singles out two areas of disagreement (food and jobs) and
provides clear examples to support these opinions, then goes on to identify an area
of agreement (TV channels), again providing support and then some development
of the example. Organisation is logical and there is clear progression throughout
the writing. There is a range of cohesive devices, used appropriately [Take for
example | Actually | Therefore | Naturally | However | This specific area | From this
point of view In conclusion]. The range of vocabulary is sufficient to show some
flexibility and precision, as well as less common items and an awareness of style
and collocation [Complex | list of favourites | fits ... my abilities | specific area
many available channels]. There is only one spelling error [beome], probably a slip
of the pen. Control over grammar and punctuation is generally good and there is a
variety of complex structures with frequent error-free sentences.

kinds. In some cases I would say that it is a good thing to have the ability to choose from a wide
variety. Take for example gastronomy. Every single person has different meals on their list of
favourites. Actually if you have a bigger family it is almost impossible to cook something that
everyone would like. Therefore I would say that it is great that you can go to a shopping center and
choose from a dozen different food types. I can always find something that looks delicious.

area is television. There are hundreds of channels, therefore you can always find something that

In conclusion I would say that we can't generally talk about choices since they could be different. In
some cases it is good to have many of them while in other areas they could have a negative effect.

This answer addresses the main features of the redeveloped sports centre, but it
could be improved by adding a brief description of the centre as it is at present.
Another aspect of the response that could be improved would be to indicate where
the various facilities will be situated in relation to each other: from the description
above the reader cannot know where for example the gym, the leisure pool and the
dance studios will be located. The range of vocabulary is above average, however:
[illustrate | reconstruction | redeveloped | additional | replaced by other facilities
renovated] and shows flexibility and precision. There is a variety of complex
structures such as present and future verb forms, passive forms and relative
clauses [the place where... | It is also clear... that ]. There could be more variety in
the language used to express future plans: [going to] is over-used.

TEST 1, WRITING TASK 1
SAMPLE ANSWER
This is an answer written by a candidate who achieved a Band 5.5 score. Here is the
examiner's comment:
The candidate has identified all the key features (hospital, ring road, new public
car park, staff car park and bus station in 2010) but the descriptions are not always
accurate e.g. [two features that still remained. This two features are City Hospital
and staff car park] whereas the staff car park was formerly a car park for both staff
and public, while the mention of the bus station is not developed. Organisation is
clear, however, with some good use of cohesive devices [According to  Apart from
The further additional features], although there is an error in the use of reference
pronouns [This/These two features]. The range of vocabulary is sufficient for the
task [two different years | features | remained | additional], though [features] is
over-used. A spelling error is noted in the second line [sourrounded] but this
does not cause any difficulty for the reader; similarly, the use of [around-turn]
can be easily understood as 'roundabout'. There is a mix of simple and complex
sentences, mainly used accurately.
Two maps illustrate the way to get to a city hospital of two different years (2oo7 and 2010).
According to both maps, the main features which is city hospital is sourrounded by Ring Road. In
these two maps, there have been two features that still remained. This two features are City Hospital
and staff car park. Apart from these two features there are some features that shows on 2olo map
but haven't shown on 2007 map. The additional features that appear on the map of 2010 are public
car park which located on the east-side of the city hospital. The further additional features are two
around-turn on the hospital Rd. which can lead to the bus station.
Overall, there are two major features that never change on both 2007 and 2010 map. These features
are city hospital and staff car park. However, there are some additional features that appear
on the map of 2oio but not on 2oo7. These features are public car park, bus station and two
around-turns.

Sample answers for Writing tasks
TEST 1, WRITING TASK 2
SAMPLE ANSWER
This is an answer written by a candidate who achieved a Band 6.5 score. Here is the
examiner's comment:
The candidate deals with both parts of the prompt and addresses some social and
practical problems that might be experienced in a foreign language environment.
Ideas are supported by examples, though there is room for further development
here. Organisation is logical and there is clear progression throughout the
response. Cohesive devices are used appropriately [Another problem | For
example | Therefore | That means ... | The second ... problem | To summarize].
There is a sufficient range of vocabulary to allow some flexibility and precision and
to demonstrate awareness of style and collocation [language barrier linked to
influence the behaviour | offend | misunderstanding | misconceptions]. There is a
mix of simple and complex sentence forms including subordinate clauses [which
means that | a person who], modal verbs [should | might | would] and gerunds
[finding a job]. Grammatical control is generally good as is the use of punctuation,
although the first sentence in the second paragraph is incomplete.
It is clear that living in a foreign country has its own benefits and drawbacks to consider. I agre
with this statement, however I think that anybody coming in another country should respect national
culture. In this essay, I would like to outline the social and practical problems.
The social problems would be language barrier, which means that a person coming from another
country might not be able to speak and understand the language which might be a problem as far
a person who is living in a country, and a person who came in the country. Another problem is
linked to the language barrier, but it might influence the behaviour of others. An individual who
come into the country might offend others with their behaviour or language. For example; some
cultures like English people prefer to be very polite and say things differently from other cultures.
Therefore a person who doesn't know how to behave in a particular culture might offend others
around him.
The practical problems would be misunderstanding of culture. That means that a person who visits
other countries does not understand other culture and he behaves as he wants to.
The second practical problem is finding a job. An individual who works in foreign country might not
be appropriate for people who he serves. For example if an individual works in a restaurant, the
people who live in a country and they were born in that country might not respect and not like the
behaviour of a person who works in a restaurant, it might be because, the cultures are different.
To summarize, it can be said that there are a lot of misconceptions which people have when they
come in a foreign country, and in my opinion and from my personal experience people should
educate themselves in order to know how to behave in different situations with different cultures.

of agreement (TV channels), again providing support and then some development

example | Actually | Therefore | Naturally | However | This specific area | From this

For millennia, the coconut has been central to the lives of Polynesian and Asian peoples. In the western world, on the other hand, coconuts have always been exotic and unusual, sometimes rare. The Italian merchant traveller Marco Polo apparently saw coconuts in South Asia in the late 13th century, and among the mid-14th-century travel writings of Sir John Mandeville there is mention of ‘great Notes of Ynde’ (great Nuts of India). Today, images of palm-fringed tropical beaches are clichés in the west to sell holidays, chocolate bars, fizzy drinks and even romance.

Typically, we envisage coconuts as brown cannonballs that, when opened, provide sweet white flesh. But we see only part of the fruit and none of the plant from which they come. The coconut palm has a smooth, slender, grey trunk, up to 30 metres tall. This is an important source of timber for building houses, and is increasingly being used as a replacement for endangered hardwoods in the furniture construction industry. The trunk is surmounted by a rosette of leaves, each of which may be up to six metres long. The leaves have hard veins in their centres which, in many parts of the world, are used as brushes after the green part of the leaf has been stripped away. Immature coconut flowers are tightly clustered together among the leaves at the top of the trunk. The flower stems may be tapped for their sap to produce a drink, and the sap can also be reduced by boiling to produce a type of sugar used for cooking.

Coconut palms produce as many as seventy fruits per year, weighing more than a kilogram each. The wall of the fruit has three layers: a waterproof outer layer, a fibrous middle layer and a hard, inner layer. The thick fibrous middle layer produces coconut fibre, ‘coir’, which has numerous uses and is particularly important in manufacturing ropes. The woody innermost layer, the shell, with its three prominent ‘eyes’, surrounds the seed. An important product obtained from the shell is charcoal, which is widely used in various industries as well as in the home as a cooking fuel. When broken in half, the shells are also used as bowls in many parts of Asia.

Inside the shell are the nutrients (endosperm) needed by the developing seed. Initially, the endosperm is a sweetish liquid, coconut water, which is enjoyed as a drink, but also provides the hormones which encourage other plants to grow more rapidly and produce higher yields. As the fruit matures, the coconut water gradually solidifies to form the brilliant white, fat-rich, edible flesh or meat. Dried coconut flesh, ‘copra’, is made into coconut oil and coconut milk, which are widely used in cooking in different parts of the world, as well as in cosmetics. A derivative of coconut fat, glycerine, acquired strategic importance in a quite different sphere, as Alfred Nobel introduced the world to his nitroglycerine-based invention: dynamite.

Their biology would appear to make coconuts the great maritime voyagers and coastal colonizers of the plant world. The large, energy-rich fruits are able to float in water and tolerate salt, but cannot remain viable indefinitely; studies suggest after about 110 days at sea they are no longer able to germinate. Literally cast onto desert island shores, with little more than sand to grow in and exposed to the full glare of the tropical sun, coconut seeds are able to germinate and root. The air pocket in the seed, created as the endosperm solidifies, protects the embryo. In addition, the fibrous fruit wall that helped it to float during the voyage stores moisture that can be taken up by the roots of the coconut seedling as it starts to grow.

There have been centuries of academic debate over the origins of the coconut. There were no coconut palms in West Africa, the Caribbean or the east coast of the Americas before the voyages of the European explorers Vasco da Gama and Columbus in the late 15th and early 16th centuries. 16th century trade and human migration patterns reveal that Arab traders and European sailors are likely to have moved coconuts from South and Southeast Asia to Africa and then across the Atlantic to the east coast of America. But the origin of coconuts discovered along the west coast of America by 16th century sailors has been the subject of centuries of discussion. Two diametrically opposed origins have been proposed: that they came from Asia, or that they were native to America. Both suggestions have problems. In Asia, there is a large degree of coconut diversity and evidence of millennia of human use – but there are no relatives growing in the wild. In America, there are close coconut relatives, but no evidence that coconuts are indigenous. These problems have led to the intriguing suggestion that coconuts originated on coral islands in the Pacific and were dispersed from there.

The typical way of talking to a baby – high-pitched, exaggerated and repetitious – is a source of fascination for linguists who hope to understand how ‘baby talk’ impacts on learning. Most babies start developing their hearing while still in the womb, prompting some hopeful parents to play classical music to their pregnant bellies. Some research even suggests that infants are listening to adult speech as early as 10 weeks before being born, gathering the basic building blocks of their family’s native tongue.

Early language exposure seems to have benefits to the brain – for instance, studies suggest that babies raised in bilingual homes are better at learning how to mentally prioritize information. So how does the sweet if sometimes absurd sound of infant-directed speech influence a baby’s development? Here are some recent studies that explore the science behind baby talk.

Fathers don’t use baby talk as often or in the same ways as mothers – and that’s perfectly OK, according to a new study. Mark VanDam of Washington State University at Spokane and colleagues equipped parents with recording devices and speech-recognition software to study the way they interacted with their youngsters during a normal day. ‘We found that moms do exactly what you’d expect and what’s been described many times over,’ VanDam explains. ‘But we found that dads aren’t doing the same thing. Dads didn’t raise their pitch or fundamental frequency when they talked to kids.’ Their role may be rooted in what is called the bridge hypothesis, which dates back to 1975. It suggests that fathers use less familial language to provide their children with a bridge to the kind of speech they’ll hear in public. ‘The idea is that a kid gets to practice a certain kind of speech with mom and another kind of speech with dad, so the kid then has a wider repertoire of kinds of speech to practice,’ says VanDam.

Scientists from the University of Washington and the University of Connecticut collected thousands of 30-second conversations between parents and their babies, fitting 26 children with audio-recording vests that captured language and sound during a typical eight-hour day. The study found that the more baby talk parents used, the more their youngsters began to babble. And when researchers saw the same babies at age two, they found that frequent baby talk had dramatically boosted vocabulary, regardless of socioeconomic status. ‘Those children who listened to a lot of baby talk were talking more than the babies that listened to more adult talk or standard speech,’ says Nairán Ramírez-Esparza of the University of Connecticut. ‘We also found that it really matters whether you use baby talk in a one-on-one context,’ she adds. ‘The more parents use baby talk one-on-one, the more babies babble, and the more they babble, the more words they produce later in life.’

Another study suggests that parents might want to pair their youngsters up so they can babble more with their own kind. Researchers from McGill University and Université du Québec à Montréal found that babies seem to like listening to each other rather than to adults – which may be why baby talk is such a universal tool among parents. They played repeating vowel sounds made by a special synthesizing device that mimicked sounds made by either an adult woman or another baby. This way, only the impact of the auditory cues was observed. The team then measured how long each type of sound held the infants’ attention. They found that the ‘infant’ sounds held babies’ attention nearly 40 percent longer. The baby noises also induced more reactions in the listening infants, like smiling or lip moving, which approximates sound making. The team theorizes that this attraction to other infant sounds could help launch the learning process that leads to speech. ‘It may be some property of the sound that is just drawing their attention,’ says study co-author Linda Polka. ‘Or maybe they are really interested in that particular type of sound because they are starting to focus on their own ability to make sounds. We are speculating here but it might catch their attention because they recognize it as a sound they could possibly make.’

In a study published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, a total of 57 babies from two slightly different age groups – seven months and eleven and a half months – were played a number of syllables from both their native language (English) and a non-native tongue (Spanish). The infants were placed in a brain-activation scanner that recorded activity in a brain region known to guide the motor movements that produce speech. The results suggest that listening to baby talk prompts infant brains to start practicing their language skills. ‘Finding activation in motor areas of the brain when infants are simply listening is significant, because it means the baby brain is engaged in trying to talk back right from the start, and suggests that seven-month-olds’ brains are already trying to figure out how to make the right movements that will produce words,’ says co-author Patricia Kuhl. Another interesting finding was that while the seven-month-olds responded to all speech sounds regardless of language, the brains of the older infants worked harder at the motor activations of non-native sounds compared to native sounds. The study may have also uncovered a process by which babies recognize differences between their native language and other tongues.

The Harappan Civilisation of ancient Pakistan and India flourished 5,000 years ago, but a thousand years later their cities were abandoned. The Harappan Civilisation was a sophisticated Bronze Age society who built ‘megacities’ and traded internationally in luxury craft products, and yet seemed to have left almost no depictions of themselves. But their lack of self-imagery – at a time when the Egyptians were carving and painting representations of themselves all over their temples – is only part of the mystery.

‘There is plenty of archaeological evidence to tell us about the rise of the Harappan Civilisation, but relatively little about its fall,’ explains archaeologist Dr Cameron Petrie of the University of Cambridge. ‘As populations increased, cities were built that had great baths, craft workshops, palaces and halls laid out in distinct sectors. Houses were arranged in blocks, with wide main streets and narrow alleyways, and many had their own wells and drainage systems. It was very much a “thriving” civilisation.’ Then around 2100 BC, a transformation began. Streets went uncleaned, buildings started to be abandoned, and ritual structures fell out of use. After their final demise, a millennium passed before really large-scale cities appeared once more in South Asia.

Some have claimed that major glacier-fed rivers changed their course, dramatically affecting the water supply and agriculture; or that the cities could not cope with an increasing population, they exhausted their resource base, the trading economy broke down or they succumbed to invasion and conflict; and yet others that climate change caused an environmental change that affected food and water provision. ‘It is unlikely that there was a single cause for the decline of the civilisation. But the fact is, until now, we have had little solid evidence from the area for most of the key elements,’ said Petrie. ‘A lot of the archaeological debate has really only been well-argued speculation.’

A research team led by Petrie, together with Dr Ravindanath Singh of Banaras Hindu University in India, found early in their investigations that many of the archaeological sites were not where they were supposed to be, completely altering understanding of the way that this region was inhabited in the past. When they carried out a survey of how the larger area was settled in relation to sources of water, they found inaccuracies in the published geographic locations of ancient settlements ranging from several hundred metres to many kilometres. They realised that any attempts to use the existing data were likely to be fundamentally flawed. Over the course of several seasons of fieldwork they carried out new surveys, finding an astonishing 198 settlement sites that were previously unknown.

Now, research published by Dr Yama Dixit and Professor David Hodell, both from Cambridge’s Department of Earth Sciences, has provided the first definitive evidence for climate change affecting the plains of north-western India, where hundreds of Harappan sites are known to have been situated. The researchers gathered shells of Melanoides tuberculata snails from the sediments of an ancient lake and used geochemical analysis as a means of tracing the climate history of the region. ‘As today, the major source of water into the lake is likely to have been the summer monsoon,’ says Dixit. ‘But we have observed that there was an abrupt change about 4,100 years ago, when the amount of evaporation from the lake exceeded the rainfall – indicative of a drought.’ Hodell adds: ‘We estimate that the weakening of the Indian summer monsoon climate lasted about 200 years before recovering to the previous conditions, which we still see today.’

It has long been thought that other great Bronze Age civilisations also declined at a similar time, with a global-scale climate event being seen as the cause. While it is possible that these local-scale processes were linked, the real archaeological interest lies in understanding the impact of these larger-scale events on different environments and different populations. ‘Considering the vast area of the Harappan Civilisation with its variable weather systems,’ explains Singh, ‘it is essential that we obtain more climate data from areas close to the two great cities at Mohenjodaro and Harappa and also from the Indian Punjab.’

Petrie and Singh’s team is now examining archaeological records and trying to understand details of how people led their lives in the region five millennia ago. They are analysing grains cultivated at the time, and trying to work out whether they were grown under extreme conditions of water stress, and whether they were adjusting the combinations of crops they were growing for different weather systems. They are also looking at whether the types of pottery used, and other aspects of their material culture, were distinctive to specific regions or were more similar across larger areas. This gives us insight into the types of interactive networks that the population was involved in, and whether those changed.

Petrie believes that archaeologists are in a unique position to investigate how past societies responded to environmental and climatic change. ‘By investigating responses to environmental pressures and threats, we can learn from the past to engage with the public, and the relevant governmental and administrative bodies, to be more proactive in issues such as the management and administration of water supply, the balance of urban and rural development, and the importance of preserving cultural heritage in the future.’

For millennia, the coconut has been central to the lives of Polynesian and Asian peoples. In the western world, on the other hand, coconuts have always been exotic and unusual, sometimes rare. The Italian merchant traveller Marco Polo apparently saw coconuts in South Asia in the late 13th century, and among the mid-14th-century travel writings of Sir John Mandeville there is mention of ‘great Notes of Ynde’ (great Nuts of India). Today, images of palm-fringed tropical beaches are clichés in the west to sell holidays, chocolate bars, fizzy drinks and even romance.

Typically, we envisage coconuts as brown cannonballs that, when opened, provide sweet white flesh. But we see only part of the fruit and none of the plant from which they come. The coconut palm has a smooth, slender, grey trunk, up to 30 metres tall. This is an important source of timber for building houses, and is increasingly being used as a replacement for endangered hardwoods in the furniture construction industry. The trunk is surmounted by a rosette of leaves, each of which may be up to six metres long. The leaves have hard veins in their centres which, in many parts of the world, are used as brushes after the green part of the leaf has been stripped away. Immature coconut flowers are tightly clustered together among the leaves at the top of the trunk. The flower stems may be tapped for their sap to produce a drink, and the sap can also be reduced by boiling to produce a type of sugar used for cooking.

Coconut palms produce as many as seventy fruits per year, weighing more than a kilogram each. The wall of the fruit has three layers: a waterproof outer layer, a fibrous middle layer and a hard, inner layer. The thick fibrous middle layer produces coconut fibre, ‘coir’, which has numerous uses and is particularly important in manufacturing ropes. The woody innermost layer, the shell, with its three prominent ‘eyes’, surrounds the seed. An important product obtained from the shell is charcoal, which is widely used in various industries as well as in the home as a cooking fuel. When broken in half, the shells are also used as bowls in many parts of Asia.

Inside the shell are the nutrients (endosperm) needed by the developing seed. Initially, the endosperm is a sweetish liquid, coconut water, which is enjoyed as a drink, but also provides the hormones which encourage other plants to grow more rapidly and produce higher yields. As the fruit matures, the coconut water gradually solidifies to form the brilliant white, fat-rich, edible flesh or meat. Dried coconut flesh, ‘copra’, is made into coconut oil and coconut milk, which are widely used in cooking in different parts of the world, as well as in cosmetics. A derivative of coconut fat, glycerine, acquired strategic importance in a quite different sphere, as Alfred Nobel introduced the world to his nitroglycerine-based invention: dynamite.

Their biology would appear to make coconuts the great maritime voyagers and coastal colonizers of the plant world. The large, energy-rich fruits are able to float in water and tolerate salt, but cannot remain viable indefinitely; studies suggest after about 110 days at sea they are no longer able to germinate. Literally cast onto desert island shores, with little more than sand to grow in and exposed to the full glare of the tropical sun, coconut seeds are able to germinate and root. The air pocket in the seed, created as the endosperm solidifies, protects the embryo. In addition, the fibrous fruit wall that helped it to float during the voyage stores moisture that can be taken up by the roots of the coconut seedling as it starts to grow.

There have been centuries of academic debate over the origins of the coconut. There were no coconut palms in West Africa, the Caribbean or the east coast of the Americas before the voyages of the European explorers Vasco da Gama and Columbus in the late 15th and early 16th centuries. 16th century trade and human migration patterns reveal that Arab traders and European sailors are likely to have moved coconuts from South and Southeast Asia to Africa and then across the Atlantic to the east coast of America. But the origin of coconuts discovered along the west coast of America by 16th century sailors has been the subject of centuries of discussion. Two diametrically opposed origins have been proposed: that they came from Asia, or that they were native to America. Both suggestions have problems. In Asia, there is a large degree of coconut diversity and evidence of millennia of human use – but there are no relatives growing in the wild. In America, there are close coconut relatives, but no evidence that coconuts are indigenous. These problems have led to the intriguing suggestion that coconuts originated on coral islands in the Pacific and were dispersed from there.

The typical way of talking to a baby – high-pitched, exaggerated and repetitious – is a source of fascination for linguists who hope to understand how ‘baby talk’ impacts on learning. Most babies start developing their hearing while still in the womb, prompting some hopeful parents to play classical music to their pregnant bellies. Some research even suggests that infants are listening to adult speech as early as 10 weeks before being born, gathering the basic building blocks of their family’s native tongue.

Early language exposure seems to have benefits to the brain – for instance, studies suggest that babies raised in bilingual homes are better at learning how to mentally prioritize information. So how does the sweet if sometimes absurd sound of infant-directed speech influence a baby’s development? Here are some recent studies that explore the science behind baby talk.

Fathers don’t use baby talk as often or in the same ways as mothers – and that’s perfectly OK, according to a new study. Mark VanDam of Washington State University at Spokane and colleagues equipped parents with recording devices and speech-recognition software to study the way they interacted with their youngsters during a normal day. ‘We found that moms do exactly what you’d expect and what’s been described many times over,’ VanDam explains. ‘But we found that dads aren’t doing the same thing. Dads didn’t raise their pitch or fundamental frequency when they talked to kids.’ Their role may be rooted in what is called the bridge hypothesis, which dates back to 1975. It suggests that fathers use less familial language to provide their children with a bridge to the kind of speech they’ll hear in public. ‘The idea is that a kid gets to practice a certain kind of speech with mom and another kind of speech with dad, so the kid then has a wider repertoire of kinds of speech to practice,’ says VanDam.

Scientists from the University of Washington and the University of Connecticut collected thousands of 30-second conversations between parents and their babies, fitting 26 children with audio-recording vests that captured language and sound during a typical eight-hour day. The study found that the more baby talk parents used, the more their youngsters began to babble. And when researchers saw the same babies at age two, they found that frequent baby talk had dramatically boosted vocabulary, regardless of socioeconomic status. ‘Those children who listened to a lot of baby talk were talking more than the babies that listened to more adult talk or standard speech,’ says Nairán Ramírez-Esparza of the University of Connecticut. ‘We also found that it really matters whether you use baby talk in a one-on-one context,’ she adds. ‘The more parents use baby talk one-on-one, the more babies babble, and the more they babble, the more words they produce later in life.’

Another study suggests that parents might want to pair their youngsters up so they can babble more with their own kind. Researchers from McGill University and Université du Québec à Montréal found that babies seem to like listening to each other rather than to adults – which may be why baby talk is such a universal tool among parents. They played repeating vowel sounds made by a special synthesizing device that mimicked sounds made by either an adult woman or another baby. This way, only the impact of the auditory cues was observed. The team then measured how long each type of sound held the infants’ attention. They found that the ‘infant’ sounds held babies’ attention nearly 40 percent longer. The baby noises also induced more reactions in the listening infants, like smiling or lip moving, which approximates sound making. The team theorizes that this attraction to other infant sounds could help launch the learning process that leads to speech. ‘It may be some property of the sound that is just drawing their attention,’ says study co-author Linda Polka. ‘Or maybe they are really interested in that particular type of sound because they are starting to focus on their own ability to make sounds. We are speculating here but it might catch their attention because they recognize it as a sound they could possibly make.’

In a study published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, a total of 57 babies from two slightly different age groups – seven months and eleven and a half months – were played a number of syllables from both their native language (English) and a non-native tongue (Spanish). The infants were placed in a brain-activation scanner that recorded activity in a brain region known to guide the motor movements that produce speech. The results suggest that listening to baby talk prompts infant brains to start practicing their language skills. ‘Finding activation in motor areas of the brain when infants are simply listening is significant, because it means the baby brain is engaged in trying to talk back right from the start, and suggests that seven-month-olds’ brains are already trying to figure out how to make the right movements that will produce words,’ says co-author Patricia Kuhl. Another interesting finding was that while the seven-month-olds responded to all speech sounds regardless of language, the brains of the older infants worked harder at the motor activations of non-native sounds compared to native sounds. The study may have also uncovered a process by which babies recognize differences between their native language and other tongues.

sentences.text: For millennia, the coconut has been central to the lives of Polynesian and Asian peoples.
sentences.translation: 数千年来，椰子一直是波利尼西亚和亚洲各族群生活的核心。
sentences.structure: 主干是 the coconut has been central to...；For millennia 前置说明这一重要性持续了极长时间，to the lives... 指明影响对象。首句以跨越千年的尺度确立椰子的生活基础地位。

vocabulary.meaning: 波利尼西亚的；波利尼西亚人的

sentences.text: In the western world, on the other hand, coconuts have always been exotic and unusual, sometimes rare.
sentences.translation: 而在西方世界，椰子一直显得异域而不同寻常，有时甚至十分罕见。
sentences.structure: 主干是 coconuts have always been exotic and unusual；In the western world 限定地域，on the other hand 与首句形成对照，sometimes rare 再补充稀缺性。作者由“生活核心”转向“异域之物”。

sentences.text: The Italian merchant traveller Marco Polo apparently saw coconuts in South Asia in the late 13th century, and among the mid-14th-century travel writings of Sir John Mandeville there is mention of ‘great Notes of Ynde’ (great Nuts of India).
sentences.translation: 据说，意大利商人兼旅行家马可·波罗在13世纪晚期于南亚见过椰子；而在14世纪中叶约翰·曼德维尔爵士的游记中，也提到了“印度的大坚果”。
sentences.structure: and 连接两条早期欧洲记录：前半主干是 Marco Polo apparently saw...，apparently 表示“据说/看来”，与事实保持证据距离而非断言确定；后半采用 there is mention of...，among... 前置定位文献。两个时间点说明椰子进入西方书写的过程。

vocabulary.meaning: 据说；看来（保留不确定性）

sentences.text: Today, images of palm-fringed tropical beaches are clichés in the west to sell holidays, chocolate bars, fizzy drinks and even romance.
sentences.translation: 如今，在西方，棕榈环绕的热带海滩图像已成了推销度假产品、巧克力棒、汽水，甚至浪漫情调的陈词滥调。
sentences.structure: 主干是 images ... are clichés；of palm-fringed tropical beaches 修饰 images，to sell... 表用途，and even romance 以递进收尾。作者指出椰子意象已被商业化。

sentences.text: Typically, we envisage coconuts as brown cannonballs that, when opened, provide sweet white flesh.
sentences.translation: 通常，我们会把椰子想象成棕色炮弹；打开后，它们会露出甜甜的白色果肉。
sentences.structure: 主干是 we envisage coconuts as...；that 引导定语从句修饰 cannonballs，when opened 是省略主语与 be 的时间状语。句子先呈现大众熟悉却片面的外观。

sentences.text: But we see only part of the fruit and none of the plant from which they come.
sentences.translation: 但我们看到的只是果实的一部分，对结出它们的植株却一无所见。
sentences.structure: 主干是 we see only part... and none...；两个宾语形成强烈对比，from which they come 修饰 plant。But 推翻上一句的完整性假象，引出全株结构。

vocabulary.meaning: 来自；本句指由植株结出

sentences.text: The coconut palm has a smooth, slender, grey trunk, up to 30 metres tall.
sentences.translation: 椰子树有一根光滑、细长的灰色树干，高度可达30米。
sentences.structure: 主干是 The coconut palm has...；smooth, slender, grey 三个形容词并列修饰 trunk，up to 30 metres tall 补充高度。句子从整体外形进入部位说明。

sentences.text: This is an important source of timber for building houses, and is increasingly being used as a replacement for endangered hardwoods in the furniture construction industry.
sentences.translation: 树干是建房木材的重要来源，而且在家具制造业中，正日益被用来替代濒危的硬木。
sentences.structure: 两个并列谓语是 is an important source... 与 is increasingly being used...；This 回指 trunk，for building houses 表用途，as a replacement for... 表替代关系。句子同时说明传统用途与环保价值。

sentences.text: The trunk is surmounted by a rosette of leaves, each of which may be up to six metres long.
sentences.translation: 树干顶端是一簇呈莲座状排列的叶片，每片叶子最长可达六米。
